subject.name: Adam Dąbrowski
subject.disambiguation: Robotics software engineer and CTO of Robotec.ai, Warsaw. Not the researchers of the same name in signal processing or space engineering.

about: Every factual claim made on adamdbrw.github.io, with sources. status: 'verified' = an independent public source confirms the claim; 'self-reported' = stated by Adam (site, LinkedIn, speaker bios he supplied) and not independently published; partial corroboration is listed in evidence. Notes disclose relationships between Adam and the authors of some sources.
how_to_verify: Open each evidence URL; the 'shows' field says what to look for.
GitHub authorship: commits, pull requests and issues are by the account adamdbrw (also older commits authored as 'Adam Dąbrowski' or 'adamdbrw').
Commit ranks change over time; they are given with the date read.

claims.claim: Lead author of REP 158, 'OpenUSD Conventions for Simulation Asset Interoperability in Open Source Robotics', with co-authors from Robotec.ai, NVIDIA and Ekumen.

evidence.shows: Official REP page: 'By Adam Dabrowski (Robotec.ai), Mateusz Zak, Michal Pelka (Robotec.ai), Ayush Ghosh, Renato Gasoto (NVIDIA), Franco Cipollone (Ekumen)'; Status: Accepted
Pull request adding the REP draft (merged June 2026)
Core schema, pull request by adamdbrw

claims.claim: REP 158 was accepted by the Gazebo PMC (28 September 2026) and the ROS PMC (29 September 2026) and marked Accepted on 22 October 2026.

evidence.shows: Status change to Accepted, by adamdbrw

claims.claim: Proposed the standardization of ROS simulation interfaces (November 2024).

evidence.shows: Issue 'Standardization of simulation interfaces' opened by adamdbrw on 5 Nov 2024; Gazebo lead thanks him for kicking it off

claims.claim: Wrote the first version of the ROS Simulation Interfaces (pull request #1: all its commits, 289 review comments), then developed them with NVIDIA contributors and reviews from Gazebo maintainers; listed as maintainer and author.

evidence.shows: First pull request, by adamdbrw (opened 17 Dec 2024, merged 21 Mar 2025); reviews include Gazebo maintainers (azeey, scpeters)
ROS Index lists Adam Dąbrowski as maintainer and author
Contributors: Ayush Ghosh (NVIDIA, joined February 2025) is now the largest committer; Adam second

claims.claim: The ROS Simulation Interfaces are implemented in Gazebo, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and O3DE.

evidence.shows: Isaac Sim tutorial: simulation control through the standard simulation_interfaces package

claims.note: The O3DE implementation is by Robotec.ai; Gazebo and NVIDIA Isaac Sim implemented the interfaces themselves.

claims.claim: Presented the new ROS simulation standard at ROSCon 2025 with Ayush Ghosh (NVIDIA).

evidence.shows: Talk video, 'Introducing the new ROS simulation standard'

claims.claim: Conceived and directed RAI, an open-source agent framework for embodied AI (2024); co-author of its PAAMS 2025 paper.

evidence.shows: Published paper: Rachwał, Majek, Boczek, K. Dąbrowski, Liberadzki, A. Dąbrowski, Ganzha; PAAMS 2025, CCIS, pp. 195–206
ROSCon 2024 talk introducing the framework, presented by Adam

claims.note: Directing RAI is Adam's statement; the public record shows him as presenter and co-author.

claims.claim: RAI is cited in later robotics research; RHO (2026) evaluates on RAI's manipulation benchmark.

evidence.shows: Robotic Agentic Platform for Intelligent Electric Vehicle Disassembly (2026) cites RAI
RHO (2026) evaluates on RAI's manipulation benchmark and transfers to RAI's ROS 2 stack

claims.note: Relationships, for transparency: RHO's authors include two of Adam's ROSCon 2026 workshop co-presenters; the last author of ROSBag MCP Server chairs the COST Action in which Adam leads a working group. The other papers are by unrelated groups.

claims.claim: Wrote the RFC and first code of the O3DE ROS 2 Gem (2022) and is its top committer in the original repository; it is now the official O3DE robotics stack.

evidence.shows: 'ROS2 Gem bare bones', first code proposed to O3DE by adamdbrw, 5 Apr 2022
Original repository: first commits by Adam (March 2022); #1 committer (104 commits, read 19 Nov 2026)
The Gem now lives in o3de-extras (Adam #2 committer, read 19 Nov 2026)
O3DE SIG-Simulation, which maintains the Gem

claims.claim: Maintainer (April 2023) and elected Chair (May 2023) of O3DE SIG-Simulation; no longer Chair.

evidence.shows: README still lists him as Chair (not yet updated)

claims.note: The election is verified; that he no longer holds the role is his own statement.

claims.claim: Quoted in the Linux Foundation's 2023 announcement on Open 3D Engine in robotics, and a panelist in the Open 3D Foundation webinar on open source in robotics.
Co-created ROS 2 for Unity (first commit and #1 committer) and ros2cs (first commit); both ship inside AWSIM, the Autoware simulator.

evidence.shows: First commit by Adam (16 Aug 2021); #1 committer (read 19 Nov 2026)
First commit by Adam (11 Apr 2020); #2 committer (read 19 Nov 2026)
Assets/Ros2ForUnity ships in AWSIM (now hosted by the Autoware Foundation; originally TIER IV)
Unity case study crediting Robotec.ai for ROS 2 for Unity

claims.claim: Led rosbag2 recording-performance work (2020–2021): optimized SQLite defaults and the --regex and --exclude options, shipped in ROS 2, and the performance report.

evidence.shows: 'SQLite storage optimized by default', merged 8 Jan 2021
Optimized SQLite defaults still documented in ROS 2

claims.note: MCAP has been rosbag2's default storage since ROS 2 Iron; the SQLite plugin and the options remain.

claims.claim: First author of the founding scenarios and requirements of micro-ROS (EU project OFERA, 2018).

evidence.shows: micro-ROS chapter of 'Robot Operating System: The Complete Reference' vol. 7, citing 'Dabrowski, A., Lütkebohle, I., Lange, R., … Reference Scenarios and Technical System Requirements Definition. OFERA (2018)'
micro-ROS is a Zephyr Project module

claims.claim: Coordinator of the Embodied Agentic AI working group of the OSRA Physical AI SIG, and an initial member of the SIG (September 2025).
Founded the ROS Embodied AI Community Group (October 2024).

evidence.shows: Call of interest, 9 Oct 2024, and the ROSCon 2024 Birds of a Feather session

claims.claim: Leader of WG5 (Simulations & Standards) and Management Committee member for Poland in COST Action CA25178 API-Net (from October 2026).

evidence.shows: 'WG5 Leader Mr Adam Dabrowski'; Management Committee, Poland

claims.claim: Independent Expert Evaluator for the European Commission since June 2018 (Horizon 2020, Horizon Europe): architecture, feasibility and execution risk of research proposals.

evidence.shows: Warsaw.ai speaker bio names the role

claims.note: The European Commission does not publish evaluator lists by name.

claims.claim: At Robotec.ai since November 2017: Technical Lead (Nov 2017–Jun 2021), Principal Software Engineer (Jul 2021–Jan 2023), VP Robotics & Simulation (Jan 2023–Jul 2024, a department of six teams), CTO (since July 2024).

evidence.shows: Quoted as VP of Robotics and Simulation, Robotec.ai (March 2023)
ROSCon 2023 talk by 'Adam Dabrowski of Robotec.ai'

claims.claim: PIAP, Industrial Research Institute for Automation and Measurements (April 2014–April 2017; December 2017–March 2019, half-time in parallel with Robotec.ai): Senior Software Engineer; software for mobile robots and operator consoles; EU robotics and space research projects; Autonomy group lead (11 people); PIAP's project lead in R5-COP; project lead and main engineer in OFERA.

evidence.shows: ROSCon 2016 programme lists him with PIAP
R5-COP workshop agenda (ARTEMIS Technology Conference 2016): project overview keynote by Adam Dąbrowski (PIAP)

claims.claim: R5-COP, the EU ARTEMIS project in which Adam was PIAP's project lead, won the ARTEMIS Exhibition Award at the ARTEMIS/ITEA Co-summit (Berlin, 10–11 March 2015); the exhibit featured PIAP's SCOUT robot and the DTI/MiR100 logistics platform.

evidence.shows: R5-COP won the ARTEMIS Exhibition award, Co-summit 2015, Berlin (visitor vote)
PIAP SCOUT and the DTI/MiR100 platform were the exhibited platforms rewarded with the 2015 Co-Summit Exhibition Award

claims.note: The award went to the project's exhibit. Adam's R5-COP role at PIAP is shown by the ARTEMIS Technology Conference 2016 agenda (see talk-2016-artemis).

claims.claim: Software engineer and system analyst 2005–2014: TLS-Technologie (2005–2007), Gadu-Gadu (2007–2008, C++/Qt client of Poland's most-used instant messenger), PZU and Inter Polska (2009–2010, system analyst), GG Network (2011–2012), DCC Labs (2013, digital TV decoding), Deloitte Poland (2013–2014, risk-rating system for Poland's largest bank).
MSc in Information Technology, University of Warsaw. Languages: Polish (native), English, German.
Volunteer maths teacher for children from families in hardship (2009–2010).
ROSCon 2016, Seoul: 'Evaluating the resilience of ROS2 communication layer', with Rafał Kozik and Mateusz Maciaś (PIAP).

ARTEMIS Technology Conference 2016, Madrid, R5-COP workshop (6 October 2016): opening keynote with the project overview, and the talks 'Modular approach to robot control' and 'Advanced and experimental human-machine interfaces'.

evidence.shows: Workshop agenda published by ARTEMIS: keynote and both talks by Adam Dąbrowski (PIAP)
Conference report: R5-COP presented results on the second day; demonstration by partners PIAP, BME and Probot

claims.note: The agenda is marked as a draft.

claims.claim: ROS Tooling Working Group, July 2020: rosbag2 performance findings.
ROS World 2021: 'Rosbag2 for Power Users', with Emerson Knapp.

evidence.shows: README: 'ROSWorld2021 talk … by Emerson Knapp and Adam Dabrowski'

claims.claim: ROSCon 2022, Kyoto: apple-picking robots demo in O3DE (demo, not a talk).

evidence.shows: Demo repository 'as presented during ROSCon 2022'; Adam #1 committer (read 19 Nov 2026)

claims.claim: ROSCon 2023, New Orleans: 'Simulate robots like never before with Open 3D Engine'; Gazebo community meeting (Oct 2023); ROS Developers Podcast #128 (Nov 2023).
ROSCon 2024, Odense: 'Agent-based AI Framework for ROS 2', and the Embodied AI Birds of a Feather session; Warsaw.ai Episode XXIV (10 Oct 2024): 'AI Agent framework for robotics'.
Davos Tech Summit, 2 July 2026: main-stage keynote 'The Blueprint for Physical AI' in the session 'Foundation Models in Robotics'.

evidence.shows: Programme data (CSV): Thursday 2 July 2026, 12:15–13:00, Main Stage, session 'Foundation Models in Robotics', Keynote, 'The Blueprint for Physical AI', Adam Dabrowski, Robotec, CTO
The talk in writing, with slides (the talk was not recorded)

claims.note: One of three keynotes in a 45-minute main-stage session; the talk was not recorded.

claims.claim: ROSCon 2026, Toronto: co-presenter of the workshop 'Train, Simulate, Deploy: Agentic AI from Cloud to Robot' (one of five presenters).

evidence.shows: Workshop listing naming the presenters, including Adam Dąbrowski
